title: Atmospheric Scattering Sky Dome Shader
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a real-time atmospheric Rayleigh/Mie scattering sky dome shader with interactive sun control and terrain reference.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a large SphereGeometry (radius 500, 64x64 segments) used as the sky dome, with side: THREE.BackSide so it renders as an inside-out sphere.
- Place a flat PlaneGeometry (2000x2000) at y=0 as ground, colored dark green (#1a3d1a).
- Add 5 simple BoxGeometry pillars (width 2, height varying 5-20, depth 2) scattered on the ground plane as reference objects, colored grey (#888888).
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 10, 50), looking at origin. Add OrbitControls.
- A small yellow SphereGeometry (radius 3) as a visible sun indicator positioned at distance 400 in the direction of the sun vector.

SHADER IMPLEMENTATION:
- Write a custom ShaderMaterial for the sky dome implementing single-scattering atmospheric model.
- Vertex shader: pass world position and view direction to fragment shader.
- Fragment shader uniforms: uSunDirection (vec3), uSunIntensity (float 1.0-30.0, default 15.0), uRayleighCoeff (float 0.0-0.01, default 0.0025), uMieCoeff (float 0.0-0.05, default 0.003), uMieDirectionalG (float 0.0-0.999, default 0.8), uTurbidity (float 1.0-10.0, default 2.0).
- The fragment shader must compute: (1) Rayleigh scattering color using wavelength-dependent coefficients (red=5.5e-6, green=13.0e-6, blue=22.4e-6 per meter), (2) Mie scattering using Henyey-Greenstein phase function, (3) optical depth integration along the view ray, (4) final color = sun_disk + rayleigh_color + mie_color, tonemapped with exposure.
- Sun disk: render a bright disk when dot(viewDir, sunDir) > 0.9995.

SUN CONTROL:
- The sun position is defined by two angles: azimuth (0-360 degrees) and elevation (-5 to 90 degrees).
- Default: azimuth=180, elevation=45.
- Keyboard controls: Left/Right arrows change azimuth by 5 degrees per press. Up/Down arrows change elevation by 2 degrees per press. Clamp elevation to [-5, 90].
- When elevation < 0, the sky should transition to dark (night). When elevation is near 0, produce sunset/sunrise colors (strong Mie scattering, orange/red hues).

UI / HUD:
- A DOM panel (id='controlPanel') at top-right with:
  - A range slider (id='sliderTurbidity') for turbidity (1-10, step 0.1), label showing current value.
  - A range slider (id='sliderSunIntensity') for sun intensity (1-30, step 0.5), label showing current value.
  - A range slider (id='sliderMieG') for Mie directional G (0-0.999, step 0.001), label showing current value.
  - A button (id='btnPresetSunrise') that sets azimuth=90, elevation=2, turbidity=4, sunIntensity=22, mieG=0.95.
  - A button (id='btnPresetNoon') that sets azimuth=180, elevation=85, turbidity=2, sunIntensity=15, mieG=0.8.
  - A button (id='btnPresetSunset') that sets azimuth=270, elevation=3, turbidity=5, sunIntensity=25, mieG=0.92.
  - A button (id='btnPresetNight') that sets azimuth=180, elevation=-5, turbidity=1, sunIntensity=1, mieG=0.8.
- A HUD overlay (id='hud') at bottom-left showing: Sun Azimuth, Sun Elevation, current sky dominant color (hex), and average luminance.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - sunAzimuth (number, degrees)
  - sunElevation (number, degrees)
  - sunDirection: {x, y, z} normalized vector
  - turbidity (number)
  - sunIntensity (number)
  - rayleighCoeff (number)
  - mieCoeff (number)
  - mieDirectionalG (number)
  - skyDominantColor: {r, g, b} (0-255 integers, sampled from zenith direction)
  - averageLuminance (number, 0.0-1.0, computed as weighted average of sky color at 8 sample directions)
  - sunDiskVisible (boolean, true if elevation > 0)
  - isNightMode (boolean, true if elevation < 0)
  - sunIndicatorPosition: {x, y, z}
  - pillarCount (number)
  - frameCount (number, incrementing)
  - groundPlaneExists (boolean)
  - shaderCompiled (boolean)

PHYSICS/MATH CONSTRAINTS:
- sunDirection must always be a normalized vector (length within 0.999-1.001).
- sunDirection.y = sin(elevation_in_radians), sunDirection.x = cos(elevation_in_radians)*sin(azimuth_in_radians), sunDirection.z = cos(elevation_in_radians)*cos(azimuth_in_radians).
- Average luminance must decrease as elevation decreases toward and below 0.
- Sunset preset must produce higher average luminance than night preset.
- Sun indicator sphere must be positioned at sunDirection * 400.

ENSURE the scene renders immediately, the shader compiles without errors, and all interactions are responsive.
physics_constraints: Sun direction vector must remain normalized (magnitude 0.999-1.001). Sun direction components must match spherical coordinate conversion from azimuth/elevation. Average luminance must monotonically correlate with sun elevation (higher elevation = brighter sky). Mie scattering intensity increases at low sun angles. Night mode (elevation<0) must produce near-zero luminance.
